issues.description: The problem statement UML and textual specification indicate orderMeal(Meal) returns void, but the solution implementation declares orderMeal(Meal) with a boolean return type. This mismatch can confuse students about the required signature and cause compilation/test mismatches if they follow the problem text exactly.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement/UML to state that orderMeal returns boolean (and document the meaning), or (B) change the solution to implement orderMeal as void (and optionally provide another boolean-returning helper if needed). Ensure tests and examples use the same signature.

issues.description: The problem text instructs students to initialize the SealSaloon attributes (including stock) in the constructor, but also states that stock must be static (and earlier mentions final). Initializing a static (and final) shared stock in an instance constructor is contradictory and can mislead students about where/how to initialize the stock field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and reconcile the instructions: either (A) keep stock as a static (and optionally final) field and instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer (remove the instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor), or (B) remove the requirement that stock is static so it can be initialized in the constructor. Update the problem statement and UML accordingly.
